text:
tanvi: Quick sync — we need to tighten scope for Optimize toolkit this sprint. Main asks: eval-triggered alerts, better quantization recommendations by workload, and a lightweight batching/caching control UI. Can we sketch launch gates?

sam: +1. Who are the priority customers for alpha? any must-haves from them?

leila: Home customers: two startups (chat assistants), 1 enterprise (search relevance). Enterprise requires rollback SLA and audit logs. Startups want simple "one-click" quant recs.

matt: On the infra side we need clear fallback behavior when a quantized path degrades quality. Proposal: eval-triggered soft-fallback to higher-precision model variant.

ash: (opsbot) nightly-eval: customers 3/3 passed concordance 0.92 on baseline. Will push per-customer deltas into the thread.

leila: Important: PM asks for launch criteria that balance econ and quality. My draft: alpha to 3 customers, metric gates: concordance >= 0.90 vs baseline OR no >3% drop in top-1, and p95 latency increase <= 20%.

matt: Agree-ish. Also need a rule for noisy evals (low sample count). Suggest: require 200 prompt samples or use Bayesian smoothing.

tanvi: Good call. Also add customer-tiering: enterprise gets auto-rollback and audit trail, startups get recommended settings + manual apply.

sam: Can we show a tiny alert spec for eng to implement?

matt: sure — sample rule: 

```
alert:
  name: eval-drift-high
  trigger: concordance_delta < -0.03 AND sample_count >= 200
  actions:
    - notify: #product-alerts, leila
    - fallback: model:recommended-high-prec
    - record: eval_event (for audit)
```

leila: Nice. For UI we need quick context: last eval run, top failing prompts, and suggested remediation (increase bitwidth, switch quant profile, or disable quant).

ash: Ops concerns: fallback may spike cost. Need per-customer budget cap and safe-guard policy: if fallback cost > X% of baseline for 24h revert to previous policy and page SRE.

sam: That ties to prioritization — we should gate per-customer rollout by usage tier. Enterprise: auto-fallback enabled by default. Startup: opt-in for auto-fallback, default to notify-only.

tanvi: Launch checklist idea: 
- Alpha (3 customers) with opt-in alerts + manual quant rec apply
- Acceptance: no >3% quality regressions for holding customers, alert infra records events and audit log present
- Ops: cost guard rails in place and documented rollback playbook
- Docs: quickstart and security notes (KMS for model keys)

leila: Timeline: ship alpha feature flag in 2 sprints, onboard customers in week 3, collect 2 weeks of eval data, then expand.

matt: Action items for eng: implement alert rule infra, add per-customer fallback toggle, emit eval_event with tags (customer_id, eval_id, concordance).

ash: Ops action: write cost-guard policy and PagerDuty playbook, add monitoring for sudden spend spikes when fallback flips.

sam: PM action: finalize customer list and consent forms for eval data.

tanvi: I'll volunteer to own the roadmap doc and customer outreach. Can folks react with :thumbsup: if they own the item?

leila: :thumbsup:

matt: :thumbsup:

ash: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

opsbot: scheduled-eval: pushed updated sample_count metrics to /s3/optimize/evals/179888/

tanvi: Great — next sync Thurs 10am to review alpha flag status and progress. If anything blocks earlier, ping here.
